question: The least common multiple of a positive integer \(n\) and \(18\) is \(180,\) and the greatest common divisor of \(n\) and \(45\) is \(15.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(n?\)
solution:
The two conditions give a short list of candidates: \(n\) must divide \(180\), because \(180\) is a common multiple, and \(n\) must be a multiple of \(15\), because \(15\) is a common divisor.

Write \(n=15k\). Since \(15k\) divides \(180=15\cdot12\), \(k\) must divide \(12\). Its possible values are \(1,2,3,4,6,12\), so the complete candidate list is \(15,30,45,60,90,180\).

Checking both conditions gives

| \(n\) | \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,18)\) | \(\gcd(n,45)\) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| \(15\) | \(90\) | \(15\) |
| \(30\) | \(90\) | \(15\) |
| \(45\) | \(90\) | \(45\) |
| \(60\) | \(180\) | \(15\) |
| \(90\) | \(90\) | \(45\) |
| \(180\) | \(180\) | \(45\) |

Only \(n=60\) satisfies both conditions. Its digit sum is \(6+0=\boxed{6}\), which is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
